## In one sentence

Speciation occurs when populations diverge until gene flow no longer joins their
gene pools, while macroevolution describes patterns above the species level.

## Reproductive isolation

Prezygotic barriers prevent mating or fertilisation, through differences in
habitat, timing, behaviour, or reproductive structures. Postzygotic barriers
reduce hybrid survival or fertility. Isolation can evolve through geographic
separation, ecological divergence, sexual selection, or chromosome changes.

## Divergence and species concepts

A biological species is often defined as a group whose members can interbreed
and produce fertile offspring. This definition is useful but does not apply
cleanly to asexual organisms, fossils, or populations connected by occasional
hybridisation. Phylogenetic and ecological species concepts emphasise different
properties and can produce different boundaries.

## Extinction and diversification

Lineages can diversify when new ecological opportunities, innovations, or
isolating barriers arise. Extinction removes lineages and can be caused by
persistent environmental change, small population size, interactions, or
catastrophic events. The fossil record reflects both biological history and
unequal preservation and sampling.

::: {.callout-tip}
Do not infer that a trait is "more evolved" because it appears later or looks
more complex. Evolution has no predetermined direction or ladder.
:::

## Check your understanding

Describe a plausible route from geographic separation to reproductive isolation.
Name one observation that would distinguish this explanation from ecological
specialisation without geographic separation.
